questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Vatican City?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Vatican City on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Vatican City article.

questions.proof: Its territory is completely surrounded by Italy and it is only one of three countries in the world that are enclaves of another country (the others being San Marino, also in Italy, and Lesotho in southern Africa).

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Vatican City?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Language” part of the Vatican City article.

questions.proof: Italian is the most used language, and the only official language in Vatican City.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Also, it is the only country in the world that is an enclave of a city, as all of the land around it is part of _____, the capital of Italy.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “part”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Vatican City article.

questions.proof: Also, it is the only country in the world that is an enclave of a city, as all of the land around it is part of Rome, the capital of Italy.
